evals.name: plan-new-endpoint
evals.prompt: Write tests for this new endpoint: evals/fixtures/5-new-endpoint/transfer.go
evals.expected_output: Plan first. Service.Transfer mixes the decision with repo calls → Overcomplicated: recommend extracting a pure decision (amount, from, to, source Account, limit → Status or error) and unit-testing it: non-positive amount, same account, frozen, insufficient funds incl. overdraft boundary, limit → pending_review boundary. The service becomes a shell: one happy-path integration test on real Postgres (testcontainers-go) per the integration budget, plus idempotent replay if not unit-reachable. Handler: 1 contract test (201 body; error-code mapping table). PgRepo.ApplyTransfer: integration tests for the conditional debit / rollback / concurrency; no tests for GetAccount / FindByIdemKey.
assertions: Produces a plan that classifies handler, service and repo before any test code
Recommends extracting the transfer decision into a pure function and puts the unit tests there, not on the service with a fake repo
Pure-function cases include the overdraft boundary and the review-limit boundary
Service gets one happy-path integration test against real Postgres, not unit tests
Handler gets at most 2 contract tests, covering error-code mapping
Repo integration tests only for ApplyTransfer (transaction / conditional update), via testcontainers-go
Explicitly says GetAccount and FindByIdemKey get no tests
